gaps.title: Manager approve/decline flow not shown in the capture
gaps.description: REQ-002 says line managers approve or decline loan requests, and DEC-003 limits this to the manager's own direct reports, with the manager's manager acting when the manager is away. The capture shows only the staff loan list (SCR-001) and the request form (SCR-002). No screen, component or flow shows how a manager finds pending requests, reviews them, or approves or declines them. This is not shown in the capture.
gaps.why_it_matters: Approval is the step that turns a staff request into a loan. Without an observed manager workflow, the approve and decline actions cannot be specified.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The spec would have no basis for the manager side of the feature. Requests could be submitted but never decided.
research_questions: What information do approval-queue patterns in internal request tools (for example leave or purchase approvals) usually show a manager before they approve or decline?
How do established approval workflows present requests from indirect reports to a manager who is acting as a stand-in?

gaps.title: Outcome of Submit request is not captured
gaps.description: The Submit request button on the request form has no target in the capture (destination_status no_target). Nothing shows what happens after submission: the confirmation, the error feedback, or where the user ends up. It is also not shown how the new request appears in the loans list.
gaps.why_it_matters: Submitting a request is the core staff action of REQ-001. The spec needs a defined end of that flow and a defined link to the status view of REQ-003.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Success and failure behaviour would be guessed during build. Staff might not know whether their request was sent.
research_questions: What do the GOV.UK Design System or similar established patterns recommend after a form submission succeeds (confirmation page versus a return to the list with a message)?
How should submission failure be communicated so that entered data is kept?

gaps.title: Date inputs do not visibly reflect the 'only free dates' decision
gaps.description: DEC-001 and DEC-002 state that an item cannot be loaned to two people for overlapping dates, and that the request form only offers dates when the item is free. The captured form shows plain From and To date inputs with mm/dd/yyyy placeholders. The capture shows no indication of availability or blocked dates. It is unclear whether availability depends on the selected Item, and how it updates when the item changes.
gaps.why_it_matters: The customer's decision makes availability-limited date selection part of the request form. The mockup's form does not show it, so the two sources disagree on how dates are chosen.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The form could be built as free-entry dates, which would allow requests for dates the item is already loaned. That contradicts the customer's rule.
research_questions: How do accessible date-picker patterns (for example the WAI-ARIA APG date picker dialog) communicate unavailable dates?
What established booking-UI patterns show item availability across a date range before submission?

gaps.title: When dates become unavailable and how clashes are prevented
gaps.description: The no-overlap rule (DEC-001/DEC-002) does not say which request states hold an item's dates: pending only, approved only, or both. It also does not say what happens when two staff request the same item for overlapping dates at the same time, or when a manager approves a request whose dates have since been taken.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours[SCR-005] 'Is availability of an item checked...double-booked?'

gaps.why_it_matters: The customer stated that an item must never be loaned to two people for overlapping dates. Concurrent requests and separate approvals by different managers can break that rule.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The same item could end up double-booked. Or pending requests could block dates indefinitely.
research_questions: What patterns do resource-booking systems use to prevent double booking under concurrent requests (for example tentative holds versus checking at approval)?
How do booking systems usually treat pending, not-yet-approved reservations when they show availability?

gaps.title: Status transitions, and who may cancel or mark returned
gaps.description: DEC-005 lists the statuses pending, approved, declined, cancelled and returned. It does not say what moves a request between them, who can cancel (the staff member, the manager, or both, and up to when), who records a return, or what happens when an item is not returned by the To date. The capture shows no cancel, edit or return action on the loans table.
gaps.why_it_matters: REQ-003 requires staff to see the status of each request. Each status needs a defined trigger and a defined actor before the status view can be specified.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Statuses could be shown that nobody can set. Cancelled and returned loans might never free the item's dates.

gaps.title: Mockup status 'Requested' is not in the decided status list
gaps.description: The captured loans table shows the status 'Requested'. The status list in DEC-005 has 'pending' and no 'Requested'. It is unclear whether these are the same state with different labels or two different states.
gaps.why_it_matters: Staff read these labels to understand where their request stands, so the wording shown must match the agreed state model.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The status wording could differ between the UI, the emails and the spec, which would confuse staff.

gaps.title: Decline reason: whether required, and where staff see it
gaps.description: DEC-005 says staff see 'any decline reason'. It does not say whether a manager must give a reason when declining. The loans table in the capture has no column or detail view for a decline reason, and the capture shows no decline step where a reason could be entered.
gaps.why_it_matters: The customer wants staff to see decline reasons, but the capture shows no place where a reason is entered or displayed.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Declined staff could get no explanation. Or the reason field could be specified inconsistently between the manager and staff sides.

gaps.title: Stand-in approver: when the manager counts as away, and manager changes
gaps.description: DEC-003 says the manager's own manager can act when the manager is away. It does not say how 'away' is determined, whether both managers can act at the same time, or what happens to a pending request when the requester's line manager changes, or when the requester has no line manager or the manager has no manager.
gaps.checklist_item: Roles, permissions, data visibility; Session expiry and permission changes
gaps.why_it_matters: This feature's approval rights depend on the reporting line plus an 'away' condition. Both determine who may decide a request.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Requests could get stuck with no eligible approver. Or two managers could make conflicting decisions on the same request.

gaps.title: Item catalogue scope and who maintains it
gaps.description: The form offers Laptop and Projector. The answer recorded against CQ-001 (DEC-001) covers date overlap, not which items exist. The requirements do not say who adds, retires or marks items unavailable, whether items are individual assets (the list shows 'Laptop L-221') or item types, or whether one request can cover more than one item.
gaps.why_it_matters: Availability checking per DEC-001 depends on knowing whether the user is requesting a specific asset or any item of a type.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The item selector and the availability rule cannot be specified consistently. Nobody would be defined as responsible for keeping the item list correct.

gaps.title: Request form validation rules beyond overlap
gaps.description: The capture shows no required markers on Item, From or To. Apart from the no-overlap rule, the requirements and decisions do not cover whether From must precede To, whether past or same-day dates are allowed, minimum or maximum loan length, how far ahead a request can be made, or how and where errors are shown.
gaps.why_it_matters: Loan date rules decide which requests managers receive and how long equipment can be held.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Requests with reversed, past or open-ended dates could be submitted.
research_questions: What do the GOV.UK Design System error message and date input guidance recommend for showing cross-field date errors (end before start)?

gaps.title: Loans list empty, loading and error states not captured
gaps.description: The loans table was captured only with one row. The capture does not show what a staff member with no loans sees, what appears while the list loads, or what appears if it fails to load.
gaps.checklist_item: Empty, loading, success and error states
gaps.why_it_matters: Every new staff member starts with an empty loans list, so the empty state will be their first view of the feature.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: First-time users or failures could show a blank or misleading table.
research_questions: What do established design systems recommend for empty-state content in a personal records list, including a call to action?
How should load failures of a table be shown accessibly?

gaps.title: Email notification content, recipients and delivery failure
gaps.description: DEC-004 decides email notifications: to staff on approval or decline, and to managers on submission. It does not say whether the stand-in manager (DEC-003) is also notified, whether cancellations or returns trigger email, what each email contains, or what happens if delivery fails.
gaps.why_it_matters: Managers learn about new requests only by email. A missed email leaves a request pending with no one aware of it.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Requests could stall unnoticed, and the stand-in arrangement might never take effect.
research_questions: What are common practices for handling transactional email delivery failures (bounces, retries) in internal workflow tools?

gaps.title: Traceability of approvals and decisions
gaps.description: The requirements do not say whether approvals, declines, cancellations and returns must be recorded with who acted, when, and on whose behalf, which matters when a stand-in manager acts.
gaps.why_it_matters: Equipment custody and decisions by delegated approvers may need to be traced later, for example for a lost laptop.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: It may not be possible to work out who approved a loan or who held an item.
research_questions: What fields do audit trails for approval workflows usually record (actor, acting-on-behalf-of, timestamp, before and after state)?

gaps.title: Whose loans the list shows, and who else can see them
gaps.description: REQ-003 says staff see their own requests. The capture does not show whether the list is limited to the signed-in user, or whether managers and stand-ins can see their reports' loans and decline reasons. Requests for another person are also unaddressed.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours[SCR-003] 'Does the table show only the signed-in user's loans?'
ambiguous_behaviours[SCR-005] 'can one be submitted for another person?'

gaps.why_it_matters: Decline reasons and loan records concern individual staff members, so visibility rules affect their privacy.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Loan data or decline reasons could be shown to the wrong people.

gaps.title: Repeated or duplicate request submissions
gaps.description: The requirements and capture do not cover what happens if Submit request is pressed twice, or if a staff member submits a second request for the same item and dates while one is pending. Limits on open requests are also unaddressed.
gaps.why_it_matters: Duplicate requests would generate duplicate manager emails, and could interact with the no-overlap rule.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Duplicate pending requests could appear and block the same item's dates.
research_questions: What established techniques prevent duplicate form submissions in web applications (for example idempotency keys or disabling during submit), and what do they show the user?

gaps.title: Accessibility of availability-limited date selection and status feedback
gaps.description: Restricting dates to free ones (DEC-001) and showing submission results and statuses raise open questions. The capture does not show how unavailable dates are conveyed to keyboard and screen-reader users, or how success and error messages are announced.
gaps.why_it_matters: This feature's main input is a constrained date choice, and unavailable dates are easy to convey visually only.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Some staff may be unable to tell which dates they can request, or whether their request was submitted.
research_questions: Which WCAG 2.2 success criteria (for example 4.1.3 Status Messages, 1.4.1 Use of Color) apply to a date picker with disabled dates and to form submission feedback?

gaps.title: Date format inconsistency between list and form
gaps.description: The loans list shows dates as '3 Mar' and '7 Mar' with no year. The form's date inputs show an mm/dd/yyyy placeholder. The expected date format and locale are not stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: Loan dates are the key data of this feature. Ambiguous formats (day/month versus month/day) can produce wrong loan periods.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Staff could request the wrong dates, or misread loan periods that span a year end.
research_questions: What date display and entry formats do established design systems recommend to avoid day/month ambiguity?

gaps.title: Ordering and paging of the loans list
gaps.description: The capture does not show how loan rows are ordered, whether past, returned or cancelled loans stay in the list, or how a long history is paged or filtered.
gaps.why_it_matters: With five statuses, including terminal ones, the list grows over time and current requests could be buried.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Staff may struggle to find the status of their current request.
research_questions: What default ordering and grouping patterns do request-tracking lists use to separate active and historical items?

assumptions.text: DEC-001 and DEC-002 carry identical verbatim text matched by keywords. It is taken as answering the date-overlap part of CQ-002 and the availability part of CQ-001, but not which items exist or who maintains them.
assumptions.why: The recorded answer to CQ-001 does not address the item catalogue.
assumptions.impact: The item catalogue is raised as an open gap (GAP-009) and not treated as answered.
assumptions.to_confirm: Confirm with the customer that the item catalogue and its maintenance are still undecided.

assumptions.text: The phrase 'any decline reason' in DEC-005 is read as not settling whether a decline reason is mandatory.
assumptions.why: The wording could mean an optional reason or simply whatever reason is recorded.
assumptions.impact: Whether a reason is required stays open in GAP-007.
assumptions.to_confirm: Ask the customer whether managers must give a reason when declining.

assumptions.text: The 'Requested' status shown in the mockup is assumed possibly to correspond to 'pending' in DEC-005, but this is not confirmed.
assumptions.why: There is no other evidence linking the two labels.
assumptions.impact: Raised as a conflict (GAP-006) rather than silently mapped.
assumptions.to_confirm: Confirm the label staff should see for a request awaiting a decision.

proposed_status_changes.reason: DEC-001/DEC-002 say the form only offers free dates, while the captured form shows plain date inputs with no availability indication (SCR-005); see GAP-003.
Mockup side of the REQ-001 conflict: the captured date inputs (SCR-005) do not reflect the decided availability restriction.
No manager approve/decline flow appears in the capture, and whether a decline reason is required is not decided; see GAP-001 and GAP-007.
The mockup shows status 'Requested' (SCR-001), which is not in the status list decided in DEC-005; see GAP-006.
Mockup side of the REQ-003 status-label conflict: 'Requested' observed in SCR-001 versus 'pending' in DEC-005.
